pharm: An oxidation product of adrenaline (carbazochrome) that reduces abnormal capillary permeability and fragility, thought to stabilize the capillary wall and shorten bleeding from small vessels, without affecting blood pressure, heart rate, or coagulation factors.
quick: Oral ~10 mg 2-3 times daily; parenteral 10 mg IM/SC (per product)
May be taken with or without food
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
Bleeding response; little routine monitoring required
summary: Adrenochrome monosemicarbazone (carbazochrome / carbazochrome salicylate) is a capillary-stabilizing antihemorrhagic agent derived from the oxidation of adrenaline. It is used in some countries (notably in Asia and parts of Europe) as an adjunct to reduce bleeding from small vessels due to increased capillary permeability and fragility - for example, capillary or parenchymal oozing, epistaxis, retinal or gingival bleeding, hematuria, and postoperative capillary bleeding. Unlike adrenaline, it has no significant effect on blood pressure, heart rate, or the clotting cascade. It is generally well tolerated but the evidence for efficacy is weak and largely historical. It is not FDA-approved in the United States and information is drawn from regional product information.
indications: Adjunctive treatment of capillary bleeding/hemorrhage due to increased capillary permeability and fragility, including epistaxis, gingival bleeding, retinal hemorrhage, hematuria, purpura, and postoperative or capillary/parenchymal oozing

dosage.d: Approximately 10 mg (commonly as carbazochrome salicylate) two to three times daily
dosage.n: Dose varies by salt and national product

dosage.t: Once to several times daily per need

dosage.d: Reduced dose according to age/weight per product

admin: Administer orally or by intramuscular/subcutaneous injection according to the product formulation
Use as an adjunct to, not a replacement for, definitive control of significant bleeding
Oral doses may be taken with or without food
Follow the specific national/product dosing, as strengths and salts (carbazochrome, carbazochrome salicylate/sodium sulfonate) differ
Do not rely on it for major or coagulopathic bleeding - correct underlying causes
moa: Adrenochrome monosemicarbazone (carbazochrome) is a stable derivative formed by the oxidation of adrenaline (epinephrine) and its combination with semicarbazide. It is believed to act locally on the microvasculature to decrease abnormally increased capillary permeability and to restore capillary resistance, thereby reducing bleeding and oozing from small vessels. The proposed effect is stabilization of the capillary wall and the perivascular ground substance rather than any action on systemic hemodynamics or on the coagulation factors or platelets. Consequently, unlike adrenaline, it does not raise blood pressure, increase heart rate, or alter clotting times. The precise molecular mechanism is not well defined and the supporting clinical evidence is limited.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to adrenochrome monosemicarbazone / carbazochrome or to salicylate component (for the salicylate salt)
relative: Conditions where salicylate is undesirable (for the salicylate salt)
Significant or coagulopathic bleeding requiring definitive treatment (do not use as sole therapy)

preg: There are limited data on use during pregnancy. It should be used only if clearly needed and the expected benefit outweighs any potential risk; safer, better-studied hemostatic options should be preferred where applicable.
lact: There are limited data on excretion in breast milk. Use with caution during breastfeeding and only when clearly necessary.
renal: No specific dose adjustment has been established for renal impairment; use with general caution and clinical judgment, as systematic data are lacking.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment has been established for hepatic impairment; use with general caution given limited pharmacokinetic data.

moderate: Other salicylate-containing products (with the carbazochrome salicylate salt) - additive salicylate exposure
minor: No clinically significant interactions are well documented for the parent compound
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory interference described; does not alter standard coagulation tests.

common: Mild gastrointestinal upset (nausea, anorexia) with oral use
Local pain or reaction at injection site

monitoring: Signs of hypersensitivity or injection-site reaction
Underlying cause of bleeding (ensure definitive management where needed)
counsel: This medicine is used to help reduce minor bleeding from small blood vessels
It does not replace treatment of the underlying cause of significant bleeding
Take the dose as directed; it may be taken with or without food
Tell your doctor if you develop a rash, itching, or swelling
Report any bleeding that is heavy, persistent, or worsening rather than relying on this medicine alone
Inform your doctor of all your medicines, especially if you take other salicylate (aspirin-like) products
pk: Not well characterized; used regularly to reduce capillary bleeding
Pharmacokinetic data are limited/not well defined
Not well established in the published literature
Dosed two to three times daily to maintain effect
Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: Carbazochrome (adrenochrome monosemicarbazone) is an adrenaline oxidation product used as a capillary stabilizer for minor capillary bleeding
Has NO effect on blood pressure, heart rate, platelets, or clotting factors - unlike adrenaline
Evidence for efficacy is weak and largely historical; it is an adjunct, not a treatment for major or coagulopathic bleeding
Available as carbazochrome, carbazochrome salicylate, or sodium sulfonate salts - doses differ by product
Regulatory status: used in parts of Asia and Europe; NOT FDA-approved in the US - information drawn from regional product information rather than openFDA
Generally well tolerated, with hypersensitivity the main concern
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: There is little documented experience of overdose, and the compound has a wide margin of safety with no significant cardiovascular or coagulation effects. Management of any overdose would be supportive and symptomatic; there is no specific antidote.
